Bug_Details:
The likely intention of a user calling Thread.run() is to start the execution of code within a new thread. This, however, is not what
happens when this method is called.
The purpose of Thread.run() is to provide a method that users can overwrite to specify the code to be executed. The actual thread is
then started by calling Thread.start() . When Thread.run() is called directly, it will be executed as a regular method within
the current thread.
Bug_Explanation: The method run() is called directly on a Thread object instead of calling start(). This is a common mistake when starting a new thread in Java because calling run() directly doesn't create a new thread but runs the code within the current thread.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the `run` method of the Thread object is called directly instead of calling `start`. This is because calling `run` directly doesn't create a new thread but runs the code within the current thread.
